event.summary: Paste sanitizing survives the helper replacement
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: considered whether removing term-bytes.js lets pasted text escape its bracketed-paste frame; source refutes this regression. Details: the new paste-sanitizer.js:26-28 preserves the removed term-bytes.js:55-57 regular expression exactly. src/lib.rs:1445 registers the new asset; terminal.js:3204 gates mounting on farhelmPasteSanitizer, :1910 sanitizes intercepted text, and :4354 supplies the same sanitizer to grid-terminal.js, whose paste listener at :1559 sanitizes plain text before paste(). grid_input.rs:576-583 independently states server-side sanitizing at the framing boundary. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, The grid client, says 'Input goes up as small JSON messages (keys, text, pastes, mouse and focus events), never as encoded bytes'. Suggested bucket: highest if a paste-frame escape route existed; could-be-highest: yes, because unintended typed shell input can execute pasted commands. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the deletion/move regression; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, behavior and callers preserved; possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not claim that every pre-existing sanitizer behavior was newly audited; the assigned change moves the same implementation.

event.summary: Paste sanitizing survives the helper replacement
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: considered whether removing term-bytes.js permits pasted commands to escape their bracketed-paste frame; the implementation move and its callers preserve sanitizing. Details: paste-sanitizer.js:26-28 copies the deleted term-bytes.js regular expression. src/lib.rs:1445 registers its asset and :1914 mounts the script; terminal.js:3204 gates mounting on the global. Intercepted text is sanitized at terminal.js:1910 and the pasteText callback at :4369 invokes created.paste; the component receives the same sanitizer at :4354 and its own plain-text paste listener at grid-terminal.js:1559 calls it before paste(). Synthesis checked multipart behavior rather than relying on comments: grid-input.js:447-477 splits already-sanitized text on characters and keeps CRLF together. grid_input.rs:223-249 actually passes each paste part through PasteText before adding framing. PasteText::byte at :623-646 strips ESC and complete end markers, retains partial markers between chunks, and reprocesses mismatches; end at :617-622 omits any held ESC at the last part. This closes the earlier premise that server sanitizing was only documented rather than implemented. Contract: SPEC_impl.md The grid client says 'Input goes up as small JSON messages (keys, text, pastes, mouse and focus events), never as encoded bytes'; server framing owns its own content sanitizing. Suggested bucket: highest if an escape route ran pasted text as typed shell commands; could-be-highest: yes for that considered route, which is refuted for this move. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, implementation and callers preserved; possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not independently certify every pre-existing terminal program's paste handling or native browser behavior.

event.summary: Removing the raw OSC 52 classifier does not turn clipboard reads into writes
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: considered whether removing isOsc52Write lets a program read the clipboard or falsely suppresses the drag-copy notice. Details: the removed helper classified raw xterm payloads. The replacement page receives completed writes: farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/effects.rs:177-188 maps ClipboardStore to Clipboard effects and discards ClipboardLoad; :207-208 delivers live Clipboard effects as notices. grid-terminal.js:1983 calls onClipboard for the model's completed clipboard messages, and terminal.js:4326-4330 increments the program-write counter for those callbacks, forwarding only the clipboard target to the write sink. Thus a read query cannot reach that counter through this event path and no raw classifier remains necessary. Contract: SPEC.md, Terminal experience, says 'an OSC 52 READ is never answered with clipboard contents' and 'Any completed program clipboard write, including a primary-selection write, suppresses it during the grace window.' Suggested bucket: highest for a clipboard-read exposure if established; other for false notice suppression alone. could-be-highest: yes for the considered confidentiality route, which the source refutes here. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, only completed write events reach the remaining callback; possible_cover: none. Caveat: this is an analysis of the helper removal and callback interface, not an independent audit of all escape-sequence parsing.

event.summary: Primary-selection writes cannot suppress the drag-copy guidance
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: after a program handles a drag by writing to the primary selection, Farhelm can still tell the user that the program copied nothing. Details: the replacement described by copy-on-select.js after deletion of its raw isOsc52Write helper depends on completed onClipboard events. The emulator preserves primary writes (farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/effects.rs:180-181), but service/grid_stream.rs:844-849 retains only ClipboardTarget::Clipboard, and :786-788 emits only that target. Primary notices therefore never reach grid-model.js:1043-1064 or grid-terminal.js:1983. terminal.js:4326-4330 increments gridOsc52Writes only on callbacks; :4426-4431 consequently admits and later displays the notice even though a primary write completed. Contract: SPEC.md Terminal experience explicitly says 'Any completed program clipboard write, including a primary-selection write, suppresses it during the grace window.' SPEC_impl.md Terminal widget similarly names callbacks for both targets. Fix direction: carry enough primary-write notification through the viewer stream to count it, while retaining the rule that primary text does not write the viewer's system clipboard. Suggested bucket: other, because the established consequence is misleading selection guidance; no security or loss-of-work route established. Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: false for this replacement-contract defect. possible_cover: none known; server notice forwarding may fall within an interface group's scope, but no coverage sources were consulted. Material attribution caveat: comparison with f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e^ shows identical grid-stream filtering and identical grid onClipboard counting. This is a pre-existing grid-path defect exposed while validating the deletion's replacement contract, not a newly introduced filter in the assigned commit; the removed xterm route counted raw OSC 52 writes, including primary writes, directly at parent terminal.js:4442-4444. Parent should retain that distinction when deciding scope or attribution. Original considered consequence preserved: removing the classifier might have exposed clipboard reads (highest), but Event::ClipboardLoad is ignored and no read exposure was found; that original route remains source-refuted. could-be-highest: only that refuted original confidentiality concern, not the established guidance defect.

event.summary: Legacy Shift+Enter and binary-byte helpers are replaced by server encoding
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: considered whether removing the legacy helpers splits Shift+Enter into submit input or corrupts high-byte mouse reports. Source refutes the removal regression. Details: grid-terminal.js:1515-1521 sends one structured key message after keydownAction filters input. grid-input.js:326 ignores composing/229 keys and :337 leaves third-level-shift keys to browser input; :363-369 serializes the key and modifiers. grid_input.rs:299-312 adds ESC to Enter with exactly SHIFT; :269-270 chunks only above MAX_INPUT. terminal-host/src/host.rs:800-802 retains each Input as a separate segment and :581-600 offers that segment whole to libc::write. This path does not use or need the deleted xterm arm/merge lifecycle. Its existing host test :4536-4572 asserts write boundaries through datagrams; this test was read, not run. Binary mouse encoding now stays on the server: grid_input.rs:747-763 pushes each legacy report component directly into Vec<u8>, preserving high bytes without a browser binary-string conversion. Contract: SPEC.md, Terminal experience, says Shift+Enter 'is sent as ESC CR in a SINGLE write' and SPEC_impl.md says 'Input goes up as small JSON messages (keys, text, pastes, mouse and focus events), never as encoded bytes'. The changed table renderer's isShiftEnterChord at grid-input-tables.js:187-191 preserves the deleted match, while sentBytes :203-209 prefixes the same CR sequence. Suggested bucket: high for a newline-to-submit regression; could-be-highest: only if an established destructive shell command were thereby submitted, but no regression route is present. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, replacement encodes the whole key and raw mouse bytes without the removed browser helpers; possible_cover: none. Caveat: host.rs explicitly permits kernel partial pty writes; that pre-existing boundary is not introduced by these deletions and is not claimed to be empirically tested here.
